item.title: Wall Street Won’t Give Up on Saylor’s Strategy, Sees 170% Upside
item.description: Michael Saylor’s Strategy Inc. is confronting a collapse of confidence almost everywhere — except among Wall Street analysts.

item.title: Aston Martin Raises £550 Million New Debt From HPS to Boost Cash
item.description: Aston Martin Lagonda Global Holdings Plc has struck a deal for £550 million ($736 million) of fresh funds with BlackRock Inc.-owned HPS Investment Partners to bolster its liquidity.

item.title: White House Official Says Moonshot Accessed Banned Nvidia Chips
item.description: A White House official accused China’s Moonshot of improperly using US AI models and Nvidia Corp. chips to create the Kimi K3 system that stunned the tech industry last week with its advanced capabilities.

item.title: The AI Export Boom That Wasn’t
item.description: Thailand’s tech exports are booming but so is its trade deficit.

item.title: French Social Media Ban Kicks Off Wave of New Rules in the EU
item.description: After months of debates across the continent, France became the first European Union member to ban social media for young teenagers this week, kicking off what’s set to be a wave of new regulations and pressuring the bloc to find a unified approach toward the big tech platforms.

item.title: Meta Taps New Chief Security Officer From Qualtrics, PayPal
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. tapped a veteran cybersecurity executive to serve as its next chief information security officer, filling a key opening after its former CISO announced plans to depart last month.

item.title: Bad Loans Threaten Argentina’s Next Engine of Economic Growth
item.description: Bad loans keep piling up in Argentina, dashing hopes that the economic pain unleashed by President Javier Milei’s harsh austerity program had already crested.

item.title: Israel Plans Crocodile-Infested Moats to Guard Hamas Prisoners
item.description: Israeli authorities are planning to use crocodile-filled moats to guard high-security Hamas prisoners, arguing that it saves money and treats those inmates in the way they deserve.

item.title: Apple to Launch New MacBook Air, iMac, MacBook Pro, Neo, Mac Mini, Mac Studio
item.description: Apple Inc. is readying an overhaul of its Mac line, seeking to capitalize on demand for powerful laptops and desktops fueled by the artificial intelligence boom.

item.title: Ghana Keeps Rates at 14% as US-Iran War Drives Inflation Risk
item.description: Ghana’s central bank joined a growing number of peers keeping interest rates higher for longer as renewed hostilities between the US and Iran bring fresh inflation risks.

item.title: EasyJet Shares Slump After Report on EU Ownership Rules Review
item.description: EasyJet Plc shares fell the most in four years on Wednesday after Reuters reported that the European Union is preparing to review airline ownership rules that it said might affect takeover bids for the low-cost carrier by two US investment firms.

item.title: Zambia’s World-Beating 36% Local Bond Rally to Extend After Polls, Citi Says
item.description: The world-beating rally in Zambia’s bonds is likely to extend if President Hakainde Hichilema decisively wins next month’s elections, according to Citigroup Inc.

item.title: Revolut Confirms $115 Billion Valuation in Latest Share Sale
item.description: Revolut Ltd. has kicked off a process for some employees to sell their shares in the company at a valuation of $115 billion, less than a year after it nabbed a valuation of $75 billion through a similar effort.

item.title: Galaxy Digital Seeks $3.5 Billion of Debt for Texas Data Center
item.description: Galaxy Digital Inc. is planning to raise about $3.5 billion from a debut junk-bond sale to fund a data center tied to CoreWeave Inc., extending AI financing’s push into the riskier corners of the US credit market.

item.title: GE Vernova Falls as Outlook Clashes With ‘Too High’ AI Hopes
item.description: GE Vernova Inc.’s shares slid after a higher revenue outlook failed to impress investors, a sign that it’s getting harder for companies that sell equipment to data centers to meet the market’s sky-high hopes.

item.title: Vale Elects Ollie Chairman After Weeks of Turmoil
item.description: Vale SA shareholders elected Manuel Lino Silva de Sousa Oliveira as chairman on Wednesday, concluding weeks of boardroom turmoil sparked by an effort from one of the Brazilian mining giant’s largest investors to reshape the company’s leadership.

item.title: US 30-Year Yield Raises Alarm in Longest Run Above 5% Since 2007
item.description: The US 30-year bond yield is trading above 5% for the longest stretch since the dawn of the financial crisis, echoing investor concerns about a growing debt pile and sticky inflation.

item.title: Samsung Says Smart Glasses Privacy Concerns Need Industrywide Fix
item.description: Samsung Electronics Co. showcased the smart glasses it developed in partnership with Alphabet Inc.’s Google, Warby Parker and Gentle Monster, offering new details around battery life and durability ahead of a release this fall.

item.title: OpenAI Plans to Spend Over $30 Billion on Georgia Data Center
item.description: OpenAI plans to spend tens of billions of dollars on a massive new data center near Savannah, Georgia as part of the ChatGPT maker’s push to keep up with surging demand for artificial intelligence software.

item.title: Samsung Revamps Foldable Lineup With Galaxy Z Fold 8, Z Fold 8 Ultra, Z Flip 8
item.description: The Galaxy Z Fold 8 has a more squat design that was built for consuming video.

item.title: LA School District Downgraded by Moody’s as Enrollment Shrinks
item.description: Los Angeles Unified School District’s credit grade was cut one level by Moody’s Ratings on Tuesday, as declining enrollment and growing costs pressure its finances.

item.title: Ireland Plans €1.5 Billion in Tax Cuts Thanks to Budget Surplus
item.description: Ireland’s government is planning for €1.5 billion in tax cuts ($1.7 billion) in its budget later this year, using some of its fiscal bounty to help workers.

item.title: Whoop Names a Former FDA Committee Chair as New Medical Chief
item.description: Whoop Inc., the maker of popular screenless fitness trackers, tapped a former FDA committee chair to be its next chief medical officer after a recent tussle with the federal regulator.

item.title: S&P 500 Fluctuates as Traders Brace for Alphabet, Tesla Results
item.description: US stocks swung between small gains and losses after chipmakers came off session lows and oil prices jumped on the escalation of the US-Iran war. Traders are also bracing for key earnings from Alphabet Inc., Tesla Inc. and International Business Machines Corp. due later in the afternoon.

item.title: NovaGold to Buy Billionaire Paulson’s Stake in Alaska Gold Mine
item.description: NovaGold Resources Inc. agreed to acquire billionaire investor John Paulson’s 40% stake in the Donlin Gold project in Alaska, giving the company full ownership of a giant undeveloped bullion mine.

item.title: Three Inflation Misses Bring Little Joy to Bearish Gilt Traders
item.description: Three consecutive downside inflation surprises and the slowest private-sector wage growth since 2020. It should be enough to convince investors that the Bank of England is entertaining interest rate cuts.

item.title: Hormuz and Heat Trigger an Asian Scramble for LNG
item.description: Some countries are finding themselves forced to buy the most expensive fuel shipments in years.

item.title: Rogers Beats as Growing Sports Empire Gives Further Windfall
item.description: Rogers Communications Inc. beat analysts’ earnings expectations as its sports assets continue providing a boost.

item.title: Nigeria Gasoline Imports Triple as Dangote Refinery Exports to Earn Dollars
item.description: Nigeria’s gasoline imports more than tripled last month as the country’s main refinery cut domestic supply and increasingly directed output toward export markets to maximize foreign-currency earnings.

item.title: Turkey Rates to Stay Put as Middle East War Impedes Disinflation
item.description: Turkey’s central bank is poised to extend an interest-rate pause, as higher energy prices driven by escalating tensions in the Middle East threaten a nascent slowdown in inflation.
